title: Make forge-bench score sheet honest about self-assessment
symptom: docs/benchmarks/score_sheet.json shows stack_score 5.0, baseline_score 1.0, advantage 4.0. All five casebook entries in contracts/fixtures/bench/forge_bench_casebook.json have hardcoded verdict fields — 'stack': {'verdict': 'pass'} and 'baseline': {'verdict': 'fail'} — authored by hand, not computed by running anything. docs/benchmarks/run_forge_bench.py reads those fields and tallies them. A DARPA reviewer examining this will immediately see a benchmark that grades its own homework.
required_change: Either: (A) Add a 'assessment_mode' field to the casebook set to 'fixture-asserted' and add a prominent header to score_sheet.json stating 'verdicts are fixture-asserted against typed artifact signals, not computed from live model execution', or (B) implement live execution. Option A is honest and shippable today; option B is the real goal. Do option A now, create a follow-on issue for option B.
acceptance: score_sheet.json contains a top-level 'assessment_mode' field with value 'fixture-asserted'.
score_sheet.json contains a 'limitation' field stating verdicts reflect typed artifact signal checks against fixture data, not live model comparison.
forge_bench_casebook.json contains a matching 'assessment_mode' field.
docs/benchmarks/README.md explains the limitation and the path to live execution.
No document in the root or docs/ claims the benchmark proves live superiority.
proof: grep on score_sheet.json for 'fixture-asserted' returns hit; no root doc overclaims benchmark result.
